topic.topicDisplayName: Hypermobility spectrum disorders and hEDS: Beighton score, management, POTS association
topic.coverageNote: Stored AGA expert review that links hEDS and hypermobility spectrum disorders with POTS, tells gastroenterologists to use the Beighton score as a screen and then the 2017 hEDS criteria, and gives a postural vital-sign definition of POTS. It is a GI-facing document, not the full 2017 classification checklist.

mcqs.question: What association does AGA best-practice advice 1 tell clinicians to recognise?

options.A: Associations among hEDS or hypermobility spectrum disorders and POTS and/or mast-cell activation syndrome
options.B: An association only with rheumatoid factor

mcqs.explanation: Advice 1 says clinicians should be aware of the observed associations between hEDS or HSDs and POTS and/or MCAS.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Clinicians should be aware of the observed associations between hEDS or HSDs and POTS and/or MCAS

mcqs.question: Does the update support testing every person with hEDS or HSD for POTS and MCAS?

options.A: No. Testing should be targeted, and universal testing is not supported
options.D: Testing is recommended solely in asymptomatic children

mcqs.explanation: Advice 2 says testing for POTS/MCAS should be targeted to clinical manifestations, and universal testing in all patients with hEDS/HSDs is not supported.

sourceRefs.excerpt: universal testing for POTS/MCAS in all patients with hEDS/HSDs is not supported by the current evidence.

mcqs.question: How should the Beighton score be used, in advice 3?

options.A: As a screening tool for joint hypermobility; a positive screen can lead to the 2017 hEDS criteria or referral
options.B: As a score that by itself replaces the 2017 criteria

mcqs.explanation: Advice 3 says to incorporate the Beighton score as a screening tool and, if positive, consider applying the 2017 diagnostic criteria or referring.

sourceRefs.excerpt: incorporating the Beighton score for assessing joint hypermobility into their practice as a screening tool; if the screen is positive, gastroenterologists may consider applying 2017 diagnostic criteria

mcqs.question: What postural finding does the update give as an example of POTS testing?

options.A: A symptomatic heart-rate increase of 30 beats per minute or more within 10 minutes of standing, without orthostatic hypotension
options.B: A fall in systolic pressure of 40 mmHg as the definition of POTS
options.C: A heart-rate rise of 5 beats per minute

mcqs.explanation: Advice 4 describes testing for POTS with postural vital signs, for example a symptomatic increase in heart rate of 30 beats/min or more with 10 minutes of standing, in the absence of orthostasis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: symptomatic increase in heart rate of 30 beats/min or more with 10 minutes of standing during an active stand or head-up tilt table test in the absence of orthostasis

mcqs.question: When should that POTS testing be considered?

options.A: In hEDS/HSD with refractory GI symptoms and orthostatic intolerance, after medication effects and simple measures such as hydration and exercise have been addressed
options.B: In every patient who reports any GI symptom
options.C: Only after a positive gene panel
options.D: Never if the Beighton screen is positive

mcqs.explanation: Advice 4 says POTS testing should be considered in patients with hEDS/HSDs and refractory GI symptoms who also report orthostatic intolerance, after excluding medication effects and trying hydration and exercise, and is not required for GI symptoms alone.

sourceRefs.excerpt: should be considered in patients with hEDS/HSDs and refractory GI symptoms who also report orthostatic intolerance after exclusion of medication side effects
